intro: July 6 (Monday) — most consequential pre-open binary cluster of the framework period. Three simultaneous determinations live today: (1) ★★ SK Hynix STOP DAY 2 CONFIRMED (KRX close ₩2,343,000 < ₩2,540,000 threshold; second consecutive close below stop = mandatory full exit at July 7 KST open 9:00 AM KST = 00:00 UTC July 7); (2) NVDA Stop Day 2 BINARY at 4:00 PM ET today (pre-market $195.33 — only $0.33 above $195 stop; determination is at official US close); (3) BTC Gate 3 (IBIT) VERIFY at 9:30 AM ET today (Gates 1+2 confirmed; Gate 3 IBIT inflow pending; BTC at $62,849 declining –$964 from yesterday's $63,813 peak — Gate 2 intact). SPCX Bond Distribution Day 9 opens 9:30 AM ET (first post-triple-holiday US session; Day 10 = tomorrow July 7 Nasdaq 100 inclusion ~$4.3B passive). NQ futures +1.55% (pre-Nasdaq-100-inclusion bid) is the constructive macro backdrop. For July 7 session: SK Hynix mandatory exit at KST open (00:00 UTC), then NVDA full-size add gate at 9:25 AM ET (if Stop Day 1 isolated), SPCX Day 10 inclusion — watch only. GOOGL and META: add on dips July 7. MU: enter at $1,150–$1,200 on July 6 open Korea-sympathetic dip.

ideas.name: SK Hynix
ideas.timeframe: MANDATORY FULL EXIT at July 7 KST open (9:00 AM KST = 00:00 UTC July 7)
ideas.idea: STOP DAY 2 CONFIRMED — MANDATORY FULL EXIT. KRX close July 6: ₩2,343,000 (–3.38% / –₩82,000 from ₩2,425,000 prior close). Stop Day 1: July 3 close ₩2,425,000 < ₩2,540,000 threshold. Stop Day 2: July 6 close ₩2,343,000 < ₩2,540,000 threshold. Two consecutive closes below the stop threshold = mandatory full exit at the immediately following session's open. That session is July 7 KST open (9:00 AM KST = 00:00 UTC July 7). Prior July 5 brief carried ₩2,552,000 as the Jul 5 reference — the July 6 close of ₩2,343,000 with –₩82,000 change confirms that the July 3 actual close was ₩2,425,000 (not ₩2,552,000), resolving the data discrepancy. Stop Day 1 was July 3. Stop Day 2 is July 6. The stop protocol is fully triggered.
ideas.why: The two-close stop protocol exists to prevent catastrophic drawdown from a trending breakdown. ₩2,343,000 is ₩197,000 (–7.8%) below the ₩2,540,000 threshold — the position has already deteriorated materially. KOSPI weakness, Korea macro uncertainty, and the broader cross-asset environment (BTC declining, chip sector mixed) provide no catalyst to reverse this trend before the July 7 open. The ADR listing on July 10 (SKHY, $29.4B) is a separate instrument and a separate thesis — it does not justify maintaining an KRX position through a triggered stop protocol. Sell the KRX position. Evaluate SKHY separately after listing if the fundamentals warrant.
ideas.trigger: SELL: full position at July 7 KST open (9:00 AM KST = 00:00 UTC July 7). Execute at market price. No limit orders on the open — the stop protocol requires execution at open, not at a specific price. Post-exit: flat KRX position. Then evaluate SKHY ADR (Nasdaq, July 10 listing) on its own merits 1–2 weeks post-listing.
ideas.risk: Mandatory exit is the action — the risk IS the exit: SK Hynix may rally July 7 KST if overnight risk-on event occurs (BTC surge, NVDA strong close above $200, global semiconductor positive news). Mandatory exit means selling into that potential rally. However, the stop protocol is not discretionary — the cost of missing a potential recovery is lower than the cost of holding through a continued breakdown below ₩2,000,000–₩2,200,000.

ideas.name: Bitcoin
ideas.timeframe: Gate 3 verify July 6 US open (9:30 AM ET); re-entry July 6 open if IBIT inflow confirmed
ideas.idea: Gate 1 CONFIRMED (July 3 UTC close $62,579.40). Gate 2 CONFIRMED (July 4 UTC close $63,015.67 — $1,015 above $62,000 threshold). Gate 3 (IBIT) PENDING: verify at 9:30 AM ET July 6 US open. BTC at $62,849.58 (11:03 UTC, Crypto.com MCP) — down $964 / –1.51% from yesterday's $63,813 peak over a 10-hour declining session. Gate 2 intact ($849 above $62,000). IBIT was in a 10-day outflow streak as of July 2 (-$40.43M); total spot ETF +$221.7M on July 3 was FBTC/ARKB-led, NOT IBIT. IF IBIT confirms positive net inflow at July 6 US open: RE-ENTRY ACTIVATED at July 6 market open. IF IBIT still in outflow: hold-watch, do not enter. Conviction downgraded from HIGH to MEDIUM on BTC's 10-hour declining session from the overnight peak.
ideas.why: Gates 1+2 provide the structural confirmation that institutional demand is absorbing sell pressure above $62,000. BTC declining $964 from the peak is a 10-hour unwinding of the overnight spike — not a structural breakdown (Gate 2 still intact). The post-halving supply shock (450 BTC/day permanently reduced miner selling) compounds daily. Gate 3 (IBIT) is the institutional demand gate — if IBIT has rotated from outflow to inflow, it confirms that the long-term institutional base is re-establishing at these levels. The declining session makes Gate 3 verification MORE important, not less — enter only if institutional demand is confirmed.
ideas.trigger: July 6 US open (9:30 AM ET): check IBIT net inflow data (Bloomberg ETF terminal or etf.com). If IBIT shows positive net inflow: BUY BTC-USD at market open. Size: 20–25% crypto allocation. Stop post-entry: $58,100. Target 1: $65,000. Target 2: $70,000 (4–8 weeks). If IBIT still in outflow: hold-watch, do not enter — reset to watch mode until IBIT confirms. Exit condition: BTC closes below $62,000 on any UTC midnight session after entry.
ideas.risk: IBIT remains in outflow (Gate 3 fails — most likely under-activation scenario; DO NOT override); BTC continues declining through July 6 US session below $62,000 on institutional return selling after triple-holiday gap; NVDA Stop Day 2 (if triggered at 4:00 PM ET today) creates risk-off cross-asset pressure into BTC; Services PMI disappoints at 9:45 AM ET (below 50 = contraction) creating macro headwind; BTC post-Gate-2 positioning is asymmetric — upside $65K–$70K, downside $58,100 stop

ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ideas.timeframe: Stop Day 2 binary at July 6 US close (4:00 PM ET); full-size add gate July 7 open if Stop Day 1 isolated

The stop is measured at the OFFICIAL US EXCHANGE CLOSE (4:00 PM ET), not pre-market or OTC. NQ futures +1.55% provides constructive backdrop but the $0.33 cushion is thin. Two outcomes only: (A) July 6 close above $195 = Stop Day 1 isolated; hold through July 7 add gate check; full-size add at July 7 open if NVDA >$200 + SPX >7,460 + VIX <17 simultaneously at 9:25 AM ET; (B) July 6 close at or below $195 = Stop Day 2 = mandatory full exit at July 7 US open, zero discretion. No averaging, no partial hold. Nicholas Parker (MSFT) field ops hire + Vera Rubin + Halos for Robotics: all intact. H200 China: policy authorization ≠ revenue (zero imports generated).

Services PMI at 9:45 AM ET (Goldilocks baseline: 52–54) directly validates NVDA's AI compute demand narrative — expanding services businesses are primary AI hardware buyers. The $0.33 pre-market cushion is thin but NQ +1.55% (which represents significant institutional demand for Nasdaq tech names today) suggests the probability of a close above $195 is higher than a close below, despite the thin margin.
ideas.trigger: July 6 US CLOSE (4:00 PM ET): ABOVE $195 = Stop Day 1 isolated; July 7 add gate: buy to full-size at 9:25 AM ET IF NVDA >$200 + SPX >7,460 + VIX <17 (all four simultaneously). AT OR BELOW $195 = Stop Day 2 = MANDATORY FULL EXIT at July 7 US open, zero discretion, no averaging, no hope holds.
ideas.risk: July 6 US close at or below $195 (Stop Day 2 triggered — most important risk; $0.33 pre-market cushion is NOT protection); Services PMI disappoints creating sector-wide semiconductor sell; China H200 import licenses not issued before August 26 earnings; NVDA intraday spike and fade pattern (same as July 5 OTC: peaked $200.06, faded to $194.83) repeats on official session; SK Hynix Stop Day 2 cross-asset chip sector negative sentiment affects NVDA close

ideas.name: Micron Technology
ideas.timeframe: 3–4 months (through Q4 FY26 earnings September 2026); entry at July 6 open on Korea-sympathetic dip
ideas.idea: Buy MU at $1,150–$1,200 at July 6 open or intraday on any Korea-sympathetic dip. SK Hynix Stop Day 2 (–3.38% close today) may create sympathetic Korea/semiconductor sector selling in US equities at July 6 open — use that dip as the MU entry. Apple/CXMT/YMTC mobile DRAM story is a MICRON STRUCTURAL POSITIVE: DoD cannot use CXMT (Pentagon 1260H blacklist) — every HBM4 wafer from Idaho CHIPS Act fab is DoD-compliant. $50B Q4 FY26 guide confirmed; HBM4 sold out through 2026. No stop protocol, no gate conditions — cleanest AI-semi entry in portfolio.
ideas.why: SK Hynix Stop Day 2 is a position management protocol event — it does NOT alter the HBM4 demand thesis or the Korea semiconductor sector's fundamental trajectory. When SK Hynix exits trigger forced selling in Korea/semiconductor ETFs, MU is often the correlated US name that overshoots to the downside. That overshoot creates the $1,150–$1,200 entry that represents genuine value: MU's Idaho CHIPS Act DoD compliance advantage is a permanent structural feature that becomes more valuable every time CXMT is confirmed as non-compliant for US government procurement.
ideas.trigger: July 6 open: monitor MU first 30–60 minutes for Korea-sympathetic dip to $1,150–$1,200. If MU gaps down on SK Hynix Stop Day 2 news: buy the opening dip. If MU opens flat or up (no Korea correlation): wait for intraday pullback. If MU opens above $1,250 (gap-up on NQ +1.55%) and no dip: do not chase — wait for natural pullback 1–2 weeks. Stop: $1,100. Target: $1,350–$1,400 through September Q4 FY26 earnings.
ideas.risk: MU opens above $1,250 on NQ +1.55% gap-up (no dip entry available — do not chase); NVDA Stop Day 2 today (if triggered) creates sympathetic MU selling July 7 that overshoots the $1,100 stop; HBM demand cycle peaks H1 2027 earlier than expected; Samsung aggressive HBM4 pricing; MU Korea correlation means SK Hynix forced selling today could push MU below $1,100 stop if sell pressure is more severe than expected
